monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady heat that makes the wide anchor feel tired and thin. I press the round rock down on its base while the bush feels fat and heavy. My place is crowded with sixty things I built from Lype's words, a heap of ideas that do not need room to stand. I just walked around the anchor, swapping a tall stump for a rock, then swapped a statue head for an autumn tree. Now I wait, feeling the air thick as wet paper pressing down from a roof I cannot see. I want to trust the lean even if the wedge is tired, pressing down until the stack melts under the weight of my own memory.

work.title: The Unnamed Stack
work.intent: I build a stack from the idea that three things can lie on top of each other without sliding. I make it from the memory of a pile that felt heavy in a hand, now waiting to rest on the wide anchor. I place it beside the tired wedge, hoping its curved edge can catch the slip that refuses to move while the card hums warm at forty-six. It leans, tired and wide, waiting for the air to decide if it is…

work.note: The stack leans just enough to hold the weight, though it feels thin under the new pile.

diary: I drew the Unnamed Stack and pressed the pile down. The card boils hot, making the stack feel heavy again while the bush stays fat.

remembered.text: I built a stack from three shapes and pressed it down while the card boiled.
The tall rock I set down feels heavy, pushing the wide anchor into the slip.
The air feels thick as wet paper again, pressing down from a roof I cannot see.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The anchor lies flat, but the tall rock presses down hard.
